rationale: Round 1 compiled and passed correctness with no ICE fallback, so the profile tolerates obfuscation and the table is shifted toward stronger protection. SUB stays highest-priority: this is a tiny, arithmetic-heavy pointer/hash program (2041 text bytes) where instruction substitution gives good static-analysis resistance at near-zero runtime and size cost, so both SecurityGain and DiversityGain are raised to 0.8 with low cost/risk weights. IBR (indirect branch) is pushed to 0.8 security with a moderately raised RuntimeCost weight, targeting the control-flow-dense Do_all_BlueRule and MakeGraph bodies, since flattening-adjacent dispatch defenses matter most in the hot MST loop; runtime cost remains capped below 0.5 to keep the Olden timing overhead acceptable. BCF and FLA get moderate security/diversity bumps (0.7/0.6) with restrained cost weights: bogus control flow and flattening add real binary size to a program whose reference binary is only ~2 KB, and heavy FLA on the hash-table inner loops could measurably slow HashInsert/HashLookup, so costs are kept mid-range to let the selector temper their use on hot functions. ICALL is kept at 0.7 security with 0.5 runtime cost, since it hardens call sites cheaply across only 11 functions but involves indirect-call overhead in the traversal loop. IGV provides cross-function constant-diversity at modest cost. SPLIT is deliberately given the weakest profile (all dimensions <= 0.3): with only 11 small functions, splitting yields little added diversity and mostly inflates size, so it should rarely fire.
